note: No AI features, so no ai_* labels. Supabase is used for login only. All data goes through Prisma on the server with DATABASE_URL, and every server action and page checks the Supabase user on the server and scopes queries by the user's profile id. The TMDB key stays on the server. No service key, no committed .env (.env* is gitignored), no seed or sample data. The inline theme script in app/layout.tsx is static. All UI forms call real server actions. The account settings page shows a 'full settings pending' message but has no fake action.

labels.what: UserProfile table is created in the Supabase Postgres public schema with no ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and no policy. The browser has the public Supabase key, so the Data API can read or write it unless the project revokes those grants

Title table created with no row level security or policy. Line 93 makes UserTitleEntry.titleId cascade on delete, so one anonymous delete of a Title row through the Data API wipes every user's saved entry for that title
UserTitleEntry table, which holds each user's statuses, ratings and private reviews, is created with no row level security or policy
CustomList table created with no row level security or policy
CustomListEntry table created with no row level security or policy
Supabase URL and publishable (or anon) key are NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables and used in the browser client. Public by design, but it is the key that reaches the tables that have no RLS

saveTranslations is a server action with no login or admin check that overwrites docs/i18n-table.csv on the server disk. It accepts any number of rows with any content. loadTranslations (56-85) is also callable by anyone
/i18n-editor is a public route with no login check and no dev-only guard, so the translation editor and its save button ship to production

The import command writes CSV values that start with '(' or 'function' (or carry a [FUNCTION] prefix, line 127) and every key into lib/i18n/en.ts and zh.ts as raw code, not escaped strings. With the open saveTranslations action, anyone can plant code in the CSV that ships when a developer next runs import on that copy

Server action rate limit is an in-memory Map per server instance. Past 30 calls a minute it only waits up to 2 seconds and never refuses. Map keys are never removed, and limits reset on each new serverless instance
The catch block returns the raw error message to the browser, and the same pattern repeats in every action (for example 413-419, 472-478, 535-541). Prisma and database error text can reach the user
Public search page calls TMDB with the server key for any visitor, with no login and no rate limit, only a 5-minute fetch cache
TMDB search language is fixed to en-US, though the app offers a zh language setting
The 1-10 rating range is set as constants here and again as literals in parseRating. Two parallel rating and review parsers exist. The values match today but can drift
